votes.evidence:
Premise confirmed by tracing the path end to end in /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215.

1. The initial leg has no identification gates. `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1110-1245) gates only on: URL parse (1130-1134), a synced+enabled `StamphogRepoConfig` for that repository within `team_id` (1138-1152), PR `state == "open"` (1166-1169), and a non-empty head sha (1170-1174). It then stamps `output={"inbox_review": {...signal_report_id, task_run_id, acting_user_id}}` verbatim from its arguments (1176-1181, 1229). Nowhere in the function is `_is_bot_authored` (defined tasks.py:124-127), a `head.repo.full_name` comparison, or `find_signal_implementation_run` called. `_upsert_pull_request` (tasks.py:319-341) only copies descriptive fields.

2. The webhook carve-out treats exactly those checks as mandatory for the same run class: `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` (tasks.py:144-207) requires `_is_bot_authored(pr)` (172-175), `head.repo.full_name == repo` (179-181), and a team-scoped `find_signal_implementation_run(...)` match plus a live toggle via the resolver (189-207). `find_signal_implementation_run` (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:484-519) is the PR-level linkage the initial leg skips.

3. The caller verifies task-level facts only. `handle_task_run_saved` (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:96-139) reads `output.pr_url` raw (98), checks `task.signal_report_id` and `not task.internal` (103-111), resolves the reviewer and the toggle (121-131), and hands `pr_url` straight to `queue_inbox_pr_review` (receivers.py:210-234 -> products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:128-158 -> `.delay`). It never checks that the PR URL is in `task.repository` or was produced by this run.

4. `output.pr_url` is caller-writable. `set_output` (products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1092-1122, `required_scopes=["task:write"]`, description "e.g., PR URL") and `partial_update` (1081-1090) go through `set_task_run_output` / `update_task_run` (facade/api.py:2137-2157, 2040-2044). `_apply_caller_output` (facade/api.py:1770-1788) protects only `pr_merged`; a caller may set `pr_url` to any URL. The only server-side attested writer is the fork-safe webhook backstop (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:171-185, 208-212) - and it only fills `pr_url` when empty. products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:71,123 documents that PR content is untrusted input for the sandboxed agent.

5. The unverified provenance disables the engine's refusals. activities.py:448-451 sets `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))` with a comment claiming both trigger paths stamp it "only after positively linking the PR to a signals implementation run"; tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:225 skips `_refuse_bot_author` and :590 skips the draft prerequisite when `self_driving`. activities.py:237-238 also skips author-familiarity for inbox runs. The initial leg also bypasses `_review_skip_reason` (draft/bot/author_association, tasks.py:210-227), `_author_lacks_write_permission` (230-253) and `_review_mode_skip_reason` (LABEL mode) entirely, since none of those run in `process_inbox_pr_review`.

6. The validator's "fork fails closed at clone" mitigation is wrong: `_clone_pr` (activities.py:946-995) fetches `pull/<n>/head` explicitly so fork heads check out fine (docstring at 955-958 says so). So an external contributor's fork PR pointed at by `output.pr_url` would be reviewed with the author-association and write-permission gates skipped and could receive a real APPROVE (activities.py:745 `post_approve_review`).

7. The PR description (gh pr view 75215, Case 1 step 4) states "A background job checks the PR is really ours (our bot, no fork, the task's repo)". The code does not. The test `test_inbox_receiver_leg_reviews_the_draft_pr` (products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:924-946) asserts only the happy path and no negative identification case exists for this leg (958-1070 cover config, dedupe, stale snapshot, closed PR).

Severity: should_fix, not must_fix. Trigger requires a signals implementation run whose acting reviewer opted in, plus a manipulated or erroneous `output.pr_url` (an agent under prompt injection with a `task:write` token, or a team member with task access), and the blast radius is limited to PRs in the team's own Stamphog-configured repos; the engine still runs a full review rather than approving blindly. The fix is cheap and mirrors the existing carve-out.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (a) "The config lookup scopes it" - true, but only to the repository/team; it says nothing about the PR's author, head repo, or linkage to the run. (b) "pr_authorship_mode is forced BOT for signal runs" (facade/api.py:3039-3040) - that guarantees PRs the run itself opens are bot-authored, but does not constrain what URL lands in `output.pr_url`, which `set_output`/`partial_update` accept from the caller unchecked. (c) "The receiver checks linkage" - it checks the task carries a signal report and is non-internal, never that the PR belongs to the task's repo or run. (d) "Fork PRs fail at clone" - false; `_clone_pr` fetches `pull/<n>/head`. (e) "The toggle sub-point" - weak as the validator said (checked seconds earlier at receivers.py:131), but the bot-author/head-repo/linkage gaps stand independently. No guard, test, or call-site fact makes the claimed gap unreachable.

votes.evidence:
Worktree: /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215

1. The receiver leg's gates are exactly what the finding says. products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1130-1181 (`process_inbox_pr_review`): parse URL (1130), team-scoped synced+enabled config for the URL's repository (1140-1152), `state == "open"` (1166), non-empty head sha (1170). Then 1176-1181 stamps `inbox_review = {"trigger": "inbox", signal_report_id, task_run_id, acting_user_id}` verbatim from the Celery args and creates the run (1225-1232). No call to `_is_bot_authored` (defined at 124-127), no `head.repo.full_name` comparison, no `find_signal_implementation_run` call anywhere in the function.

2. The webhook carve-out for the SAME run class does all three positively: tasks.py:169-171 (`_is_bot_authored`), 175-178 (head repo == base repo, "Fork-safety"), 190-198 (`find_signal_implementation_run` + team recheck), 199-206 (toggle re-check). So the two "linkage-verified trigger paths" are asymmetric.

3. The stamped flag disables real gates without re-verification. products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:448-451 sets `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))` with a comment claiming both paths stamp it "only after positively linking the PR to a signals implementation run". tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:225 (`if self.pr.author_is_bot and not self.self_driving: return self._refuse_bot_author()`) and :590 (draft prerequisite skipped when `self_driving`). tasks.py:944 shows inbox runs also bypass `_review_mode_skip_reason`. Approval is posted at activities.py:745 (`post_approve_review`).

4. The upstream input is agent-controlled, not server-derived. `output.pr_url` is written by the sandbox through `PATCH runs/<id>/set_output` (products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1101-1120). `validate_set_output` (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2123-2136) only checks the task's `json_schema`; `set_task_run_output` (2139-2160) saves whatever `pr_url` string arrives, which fires review_hog's post_save receiver. That receiver (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:93-105) checks only `task.signal_report_id` and `task.internal` — task-level facts — then queues stamphog with `pr_url` at 127-138. The fork-safe backstop at products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:178-185 only fills `pr_url` when empty; it never validates an agent-supplied one.

5. The validator's claimed fork mitigation is wrong: `_clone_pr` (activities.py:956-959) fetches the head via `pull/<n>/head` precisely so fork heads clone, so a fork PR does not fail closed at clone time.

6. Existing tests do not cover the claim on this leg. products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:891-1000: `_run_inbox_task`/`_inbox_pr` use only a bot-authored (`posthog-code[bot]`, type Bot) fixture at 916; the three receiver-leg tests (`test_inbox_receiver_leg_reviews_the_draft_pr`, `..._noops_without_a_reviewable_config`, `..._refires_dedupe_on_the_current_head`) assert config gating and dedupe only. The fork/unlinked negative tests (`fork_head_is_never_linked` at 842, unlinked at 880-888) exercise the webhook carve-out, not `process_inbox_pr_review`.

7. The PR's own contract contradicts the code: PR #75215 body step 4 says "A background job checks the PR is really ours (our bot, no fork, the task's repo)"; products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:97-98 says the flag is stamped by "only the two linkage-verified trigger paths".

Severity should_fix: the reachable trigger needs a misbehaving or prompt-injected agent inside a signal implementation run (a threat this codebase explicitly designs against), and blast radius is limited to open PRs in repos the same team has a synced+enabled Stamphog config for; but the consequence is a genuine GitHub APPROVE minted on a PR that cleared no identification gate, with the bot-author, draft, and review-mode gates deliberately disabled. The fix is cheap and mirrors the carve-out.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (a) "the receiver already links the PR" — it checks task.signal_report_id/task.internal only (receivers.py:98-105), never that pr_url names this task's repo or branch; (b) "set_output validates pr_url" — validate_set_output only runs jsonschema against task.json_schema (facade/api.py:2131-2135), no repo/branch check; (c) "the webhook backstop is fork-safe" — it only fills an EMPTY pr_url (webhooks.py:178-185) and cannot override an agent-written one; (d) "the config lookup scopes it" — it only requires the URL's repo to be one the team enabled, which is exactly the set of repos where an approval matters; (e) "a fork PR fails at clone" — _clone_pr fetches pull/<n>/head (activities.py:956-959) so forks clone fine; (f) "tests cover it" — no receiver-leg test uses a human-authored, fork-headed, or unlinked PR (test_tasks.py:891-1000). The one sub-point that does not hold up is the toggle re-check: review_hog evaluates it synchronously at queue time (receivers.py:126) seconds before the Celery task runs, so that part is weak; the bot-author/head-repo/linkage gap is the load-bearing defect.

votes.evidence:
Trigger is reachable in production configuration; no gate on the path identifies the PR.

Writer of `output.pr_url` is unvalidated and reachable from the sandbox:
- `posthog/temporal/oauth.py:37-38` — `INTERNAL_SCOPES` always includes `"task:write"`, so every sandboxed agent token (`start_agent_server.py:199`, `resolve_scopes` at oauth.py:115-119) can call the run-update endpoints.
- `products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1097-1119` — `set_output` (`required_scopes=["task:write"]`) and `partial_update` (api.py:1080-1094) take `output` verbatim.
- `products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2140-2160` (`set_task_run_output`) and `:1773-1788` (`_apply_caller_output`) only strip webhook-attested keys; nothing compares `pr_url` to `task.repository`.
- `products/tasks/backend/temporal/code_workstreams/activities/load_pr_urls.py:26-31` documents exactly this: "`output.pr_url` is user-writable ... a user could point `pr_url` at an arbitrary PR the installation can see", and that consumer defends itself with `_pr_url_belongs_to_task_repo`. The stamphog receiver leg has no equivalent.

Receiver forwards it unverified:
- `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:93-136` — checks only `task.signal_report_id is not None`, `not task.internal`, and the acting reviewer's `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` toggle, then passes `pr_url` straight to `_start_stamphog_review` → `queue_inbox_pr_review` (stamphog `facade/api.py:128-153`).

`process_inbox_pr_review` never identifies the PR:
- `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1130-1174` — gates are parse, team-scoped enabled config for the URL's repo (`repository__iexact`), `state == "open"`, non-empty head sha. No `_is_bot_authored(pr)`, no `head.repo.full_name` check, no `find_signal_implementation_run`, no `_review_mode_skip_reason`. It stamps `output={"inbox_review": ...}` at tasks.py:1176-1236 from caller-supplied ids.
- Contrast the webhook carve-out at tasks.py:169-207, which requires all of these for the identical run class, and `products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:96-100`, which claims the provenance is stamped "only [by] the two linkage-verified trigger paths" — the receiver leg verifies task-level linkage, not PR-level.

The provenance flag disables every downstream identification gate:
- `products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:448-451` — `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))`.
- `tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:225-226` skips `_refuse_bot_author`; `:590` skips the draft prerequisite; activities.py:237-238 skips the author familiarity fetch. AGENTS.md:110 confirms these runs also bypass review-mode and author-write-permission gates.
- The validator's "fork fails at clone" mitigation is wrong: `_clone_pr` fetches `pull/<n>/head` (activities.py:989, docstring 955-957 says this is specifically so fork heads resolve). So a repo-native human PR AND a fork PR both clone fine and reach a real APPROVE.

Prod exposure: the toggle is a plain user setting with no feature-flag gate found (`products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:27`, `CodeReviewScene.tsx:1061-1066`); it needs only a synced+enabled Stamphog config. Tests only ever use a bot-authored fixture (`test_tasks.py:908-920`); nothing covers a human-authored PR on this leg.

Preconditions for the trigger: team with Stamphog App installed and an enabled config for repo R; an acting reviewer with the toggle on; a signal-report implementation run in that team whose sandbox agent (prompt-injected by repo content, which `products/stamphog/CLAUDE.md` treats as untrusted) or any `task:write` holder writes `output.pr_url` to another open PR in R. Result: the team's Stamphog App posts a genuine APPROVE on a PR nobody identified as self-driving. Blast radius is one team's own configured repos, which is why should_fix rather than must_fix; the fix is cheap and mirrors the carve-out.
votes.refutation:
Attempts to refute, all failed except one sub-point:
1. "The agent always opens the PR against `task.repository`, so `pr_url` is trustworthy" — the write path has no such check (facade/api.py:2140-2160, :1773-1788), and `load_pr_urls.py:26-31` explicitly treats the field as user-writable/untrusted.
2. "`pr_authorship_mode` is forced BOT for signal runs (facade/api.py:4409-4411)" — that controls how the agent opens ITS PR, not what value lands in `output.pr_url`; it does not constrain a manipulated or erroneous write.
3. "The webhook backstop is fork-safe (webhooks.py:178-185)" — it only writes `pr_url` when unset (`_record_run_output_field` returns False otherwise, webhooks.py:283-290) and never validates an agent-set value.
4. "A fork PR fails at clone time" — false; `_clone_pr` fetches `pull/<n>/head` (activities.py:989), so fork heads resolve.
5. "The sandbox token can't reach `set_output`" — false; `task:write` is in `INTERNAL_SCOPES` (oauth.py:37).
6. The toggle re-check sub-point (suggestion item 4) IS weak: `handle_task_run_saved` checks `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` synchronously at receivers.py:126 and the Celery hop is seconds; a mid-flight flip is a narrow race and the webhook path already re-checks on later heads. That sub-point alone would not make the finding real; the bot-author / head-repo / linkage checks are the load-bearing gap.
